trimmedBy: node trim-ats-a-captures.mjs (JSON.parse, whole-record selection by job id (meta.total rewritten to the kept count so the envelope stays self-consistent), regex redaction of e-mail addresses and separator-bearing phone numbers inside string values, JSON.stringify, prettier); never a byte cut
notes: 720 jobs captured, 4 kept: two multi-location strings ("US-Chicago, US-New York", "Seattle, New York, San Francisco"), a single city, and one with first_published equal to updated_at. Whole response 5.6 MB, 69,266 JSON nodes. OWNERSHIP VERIFIED from the payload: company_name is "Stripe" on 720 of 720 jobs; absolute_url is a company-hosted page (https://stripe.com/jobs/search?gh_jid=N) where gh_jid is the only identity in the URL. Documented (https://docs.greenhouse.io/job-board.html): GET endpoints need no authentication ("Job Board data is publicly available"); only the application POST needs Basic auth. robots.txt of boards-api.greenhouse.io: User-agent * / Disallow: /embed/ only, so /v1/boards/{token}/jobs is allowed. The docs state no rate limit or terms of use. Job content is HTML-escaped by Greenhouse (entities) and the adapter decodes it once. company_name and first_published appear on every job of this response although the docs show them only in the single-job example. E-mail addresses and phone numbers inside string values were replaced by a parser; personal NAMES in free-text descriptions cannot be found by a parser and were not redacted (records were chosen with short descriptions to limit exposure).
